mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within the last month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which can lead to reduced consumer spending and lower corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in real estate sales (HOUST) signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which can lead to reduced consumer spending and lower corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of declining HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% within the last month indicates supply-side disruptions, leading to reduced output and higher prices, which can negatively impact corporate earnings and result in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO drops and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals strengthening consumer demand, which can lead to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between RSAFS increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 within the last month, it signals a strengthening labor market, which can lead to increased consumer spending and higher corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases > 0.3% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint effect of UNRATE decrease and PAYEMS increase on positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure combined with tight monetary policy, leading to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and increasing CPIAUCSL on negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) increases by more than 2% and real GDP (GDPC1) increases by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter, it signals a strong supply-side expansion, which can lead to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases > 2% and GDPC1 increases > 1% quarter-over-quarter
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint effect of INDPRO and GDPC1 increases on positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
